assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology led from the identification of GLP-1 as a glucose-dependent insulinotropic hormone to long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. The physiological insight is original and the medical and societal impact is very large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor action, intestinotrophic GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a plausible three-person set. Knudsen (drug design, liraglutide and semaglutide) is an industrial contribution that could be argued for instead; Habener-type contributions are not on the credited list. Allocation among peptide discovery, physiology and drug development is contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large outcome trials for cardiovascular, renal and weight outcomes. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mojsov's priority relative to others in early GLP-1 sequence work is disputed and I have not verified details.
Whether a prize would favor basic physiology or drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling in which ER stress is sensed by IRE1 and transmitted through HAC1/XBP1 splicing. It is conceptually clean, fundamental, and underlies understanding of secretory-cell function, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter (IRE1 mechanism, unconventional splicing, ISRIB-related work) and Mori (identification of the UPR transcriptional response, HAC1/ATF6) are the natural pair. Other contributors such as Ron and Kaufman (PERK/eIF2alpha arm) are not on the credited list, so the credit is potentially incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed in yeast and mammals over three decades, with high-profile prior recognition. Clinical translation is still limited, but basic maturity is high.
uncertainties: Whether the PERK/ATF6 branches deserve co-recognition is unresolved.
Therapeutic payoff is modest so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The concept, engineering and clinical proof are all significant.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB, first patients) and Sadelain (second-generation CAR design, CD28 costimulation, preclinical proof) are central. Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy and early clinical CAR work is a credible third name; early inventors such as Eshhar are not on the credited list, so the allocation is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multiyear remissions. Solid-tumor application, toxicity and manufacturing remain open, but the core discovery is mature and its impact is evident.
uncertainties: Priority among Eshhar, Sadelain, June and others requires careful adjudication.
Late effects such as secondary malignancy and limited benefit in solid tumors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR in yeast and mTOR as the central controller of growth in response to nutrients and growth factors reshaped cell physiology, metabolism, ageing and cancer biology. It is a fundamental, widely connected finding with clear lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined it as the rapamycin target and the growth regulator. Schreiber contributed the chemical-biology work on FKBP12-rapamycin and the mammalian target, and Sabatini mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work. A prize built on Hall alone, or Hall with one other, is plausible; I have not independently weighed Schreiber against Sabatini.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across eukaryotes with a large independent literature and approved rapalogs in transplantation and oncology. Highly mature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the yeast genetics, the pharmacology and the mammalian pathway is unresolved.
Sabatini's inclusion could be complicated by non-scientific considerations that I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provides cell-type-specific, millisecond control of excitable cells and has transformed causal neuroscience and physiology. The discovery of channelrhodopsins and their transfer to neurons is original and the methodological impact is enormous.
assessment.attribution: The prize allocation is the main difficulty with six credited names. Hegemann and Nagel (with Bamberg) identified channelrhodopsin function; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenböck made earlier genetically targeted photostimulation. I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel as one possible set, noting Boyden and Bamberg have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated across thousands of studies and still extended to clinical vision restoration. A methods prize is within Nobel precedent, but the credit disputes make timing less certain.
uncertainties: Boyden versus Nagel versus Bamberg is contested.
Direct therapeutic impact is just emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing converts an RNA-processing mechanism into a disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a clear bench-to-bedside discovery that also validated splice-switching oligonucleotides generally.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing work and identification of ISS-N1 target sequences with the oligonucleotide concept) and Bennett (chemistry and development of nusinersen at Ibis/Ionis) form a coherent pair. Other contributors to the SMN2 splicing targets, such as Singh and Singh, are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong long-term outcomes in infants. Recognition would be timely, though the platform is still young compared with earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Credit for the specific target site relative to groups outside the credited list is uncertain.
Balance between basic discovery and industrial development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV demonstrated prevention of persistent infection and cervical neoplasia, with real-world evidence of population-level cancer prevention. This is a landmark in preventive cancer medicine.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP assembly and immunogenicity), and Frazer (with Zhou, VLP expression and development) are the central credited names. Other contributors, including Zhou (deceased) and Kirnbauer, make the full allocation complicated.
assessment.maturity: Strong evidence from trials and national programmes of reduced HPV infection and cervical lesions, with emerging cancer-incidence data. Zur Hausen already received a Nobel for HPV and cervical cancer, so a second HPV-related award may be seen as overlapping.
uncertainties: Prior HPV-related prize may reduce the appetite for recognition.
Attribution among VLP developers is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL created the paradigm for oncogene-directed therapy and turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a plausible trio. Rowley and Witte for the translocation and BCR-ABL are outside the credited names, so the allocation is partial.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of evidence and ongoing survival data. The concept is mature, though the claim to novelty may be diluted by later targeted therapies.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the discovery as fully recognized by Lasker awards.
Fair credit for the underlying cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries.
